reading: Three colour bands sit side by side in every row (left colour, middle colour, right colour). In each row the middle-colour run slides left until its right end sits on the leftmost right end of all middle runs (or until it starts at column 0). The left-colour cells it passes over fill in to its right. The right band does not change.

slots.subject: the middle-colour run in each row (it keeps its length)
slots.target: the column E = the minimum, over all rows, of the middle run's right end; the run moves to end at E, or to start at column 0 if it is longer than E+1
slots.fill: the left-colour cells keep their count: those not left of the run's new start go right after the run

why: on every pair each output row has the same number of each colour as its input row, and the middle run ends at min-right-end unless that would push it past column 0

reading: One rectangle is joined to a second rectangle by a straight tether one cell wide, in the first rectangle's colour. The tether is erased and the rectangle slides along the tether's direction by the tether's length, so it ends up touching the second rectangle.

slots.subject: the body of the tethered object (its cells minus the one-cell-wide line)
slots.tether: the one-cell-wide straight line of the subject's colour that touches the other object
slots.target: the other (untethered) object; the move stops in contact with it
slots.distance: the tether's length, along the tether's direction

why: the body keeps its shape and ends exactly where the tether used to end, touching the target object

reading: Columns of 0 split the input into three 4x4 panels of 5. The hole pattern in each panel maps to a colour: solid→2, centre hole→8, bottom-centre notch→4, side notches in rows 1-2→3. The output is 3x3: row i is filled with panel i's colour.

slots.panels: the three 4x4 stripes cut by the all-0 separator columns
slots.key: a pattern→colour table learned from training: solid=2, 2x2 centre hole=8, 2x2 hole at bottom centre=4, left and right notches in the middle rows=3
slots.output: a 3x3 grid; row i is all key(panel i)

why: on every pair each output row is uniform, and its colour depends only on the hole pattern of the matching panel
invariants: one output row per panel, in left-to-right order

reading: Each isolated coloured cell draws a line in its own colour to the right border. The line then turns down along the last column and stops on the row just above the next marker (counting markers by row) or at the bottom of the grid.

slots.source: markers (isolated single cells), handled in row order
slots.path: horizontal ray to the right border, then down the last column
slots.stop: the row just above the next marker's row, or the grid bottom for the last marker

why: every marker row is filled from the marker to the right edge, and each part of the right column takes the colour of the closest marker above it

reading: A hollow box has four sides of four different colours. A separate 8-shape has the same size as the box's interior. The output is the box cut out with the 8-shape placed inside it. Each 8 cell becomes the colour of the strictly nearest side; a cell equally near two sides stays 8.
verb: fit and colour by nearest side

slots.container: the box whose 4 sides are 4 single colours (corners 0); its box is the output
slots.content: the 8-coloured object, whose bounding box equals the container's interior; pasted aligned to its box
slots.key: per 8 cell: the side colour at minimum distance (top/bottom by row, left/right by column); ties stay 8

why: the output is the container's box; its interior non-0 cells are exactly the 8-shape's cells, coloured by the strictly nearest side
invariants: the container's four sides and empty corners

reading: A colour histogram. Each input colour becomes one output column, ordered from most frequent to least. The column is filled from the top for as many cells as that colour has, and the rest is 0. Output height = the largest count; output width = the number of colours.

slots.bars: one column per distinct colour, sorted by pixel count, descending
slots.length: the colour's pixel count, filled from row 0 downward
slots.size: height = the maximum pixel count, width = the number of colours; empty cells 0

why: on every pair column j holds the j-th most frequent colour exactly count times, top-aligned

reading: The grid is split into a block of 8 and a block of 1. The colour-2 pieces inside them slide horizontally, row by row: in the 8 block they go left to that block's edge, and in the 1 block they go right to that block's edge. The block colour fills in behind them.

slots.subject: the colour-2 cells (pieces keep their shape)
slots.regions: the two solid rectangular areas of colour 8 and colour 1
slots.direction: learned per region colour: left on 8, right on 1
slots.stop: the edge of the region (the grid border or the boundary with the other region)

why: each row segment of a region keeps its count of 2s, packed against the region's left edge for 8 and its right edge for 1
invariants: per-row count of 2s in each region

reading: There are two nested-rectangle structures, each an outer block with an inner rectangle. The inner rectangle's edge has defects: notches of the outer colour cut into it, or bumps of the inner colour sticking out. Each defect becomes a two-cell domino straddling the edge (the defect cell plus its neighbour across the edge), coloured with the OTHER structure's outer colour.

slots.structures: the two outer rectangles, each holding one or more inner rectangles
slots.subject: the defect cells on an inner rectangle's border: a notch (outer colour inside the inner box) or a bump (inner colour just outside it)
slots.unit: a 2-cell domino perpendicular to the edge: the defect cell plus the adjacent cell on the other side of the edge line
slots.colour: the outer colour of the other structure

why: every changed cell lies in such a domino, and every defect gets one
invariants: all cells away from the defects

reading: Each colour-3 cell slides left along its row, row by row, until the next cell is 8 or the grid border. The cells it leaves become 0. The 8s never move.

slots.subject: the colour-3 cells, each row's run moved on its own (vertical 3-shapes do not move together)
slots.stop: the first 8 cell to the left, or column 0

why: in each row the 3s end packed against the nearest 8 or border to their left, with the same count

reading: Find each 5 cell whose eight neighbours are all non-zero (2 or 5) and which gathers a cluster of 2s around it. Process them greedily, most 2s first, taking a cell only if its 2s are not yet claimed. That centre becomes 4, the 5s in its ring become 7, and the 2s stay.

slots.centre: a 5 cell whose 8 neighbours contain no 0 and include at least one 2; chosen greedily by the number of ring 2s, each 2 claimed at most once
slots.scope: every 2 cell of the grid ends up in exactly one chosen ring

why: every changed cell lies in the 3x3 window of a chosen centre, and the window holds no 0
